simple.meaning: מַעֲמָק (maʻămâq) is a Hebrew word meaning “a deep.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַעֲמָק (H4615) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 69:3, with occurrences in Psalms, Isaiah, Ezekiel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַעֲמָק (H4615) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַעֲמָק (H4615) before moving outward to related references.

occurrences.englishText: I am weary with my crying.
Don’t let the flood waters overwhelm me,
Out of the depths I have cried to you, Yahweh.
Isn’t it you who dried up the sea,
In the time that you were broken by the seas,
